content.value: Nested loops visit the cells of a two-dimensional array. Row-major order puts the row loop outside; column-major order puts the column loop outside. Use each row length for row-major traversal, and state rectangular-array assumptions for column-major algorithms. Enhanced loops can aggregate cells without explicit indices.
For {{1, 2, 3}, {4, 5, 6}}, this prints 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Reversing the nesting for column-major order prints 1, 4, 2, 5, 3, 6. Reset the inner counter for every outer iteration.
Practice: trace the example by hand, change one input, and explain how the result changes. Check an empty or boundary case when the preconditions allow it.
